subject: Erroneous sleep data returned from low activity signal

messages.author: 39e7047f486b40ef
messages.subject: Erroneous sleep data returned from low activity signal
parts:
I have activity data recorded over multiple days. During a subset of days, say days 4 to 12, the actigraph was either not worn or malfunctioned resulting in very low magnitude ENMO (mean < 0.1 with random spikes = 0.4). We did not use a sleep diary. For all nights during the "bad" period, we get the exact same sleep/wake up detection periods displayed between approximately midnight to 8am night after night. Any idea what would be causing this problem? We will of course ignore these nights from our analyses, but are wondering why an exact pattern repeats itself.

Thanks for your help,

Phil

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Erroneous sleep data returned from low activity signal
parts:
Hi Phil,

Sorry, I have ignored all GGIR e-mail traffic for a couple of months to focus more on new developments.
What you saw is the imputed data. This is clarified in the visualisation of part2, while non-wear time is not visualised at the moment in the other visualisations produced by GGIR.
When you are unsure about whether to include or exclude data always look out for variables related to non-wear time or valid hours, rather than judging the data on the plausibility of its value alone. Additionally, it is good checking out the calibration error reported in the part2 output.

Cheers,

Vincent
